solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speciality shop absolutely makes distribution

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling speciality foods
absolutely and very both work as intensifiers

explanation.surface: A specialist food shop that thoroughly organises its distribution network.
explanation.definitionFit: Distribution of goods or post is the business of handing them over, which is a delivery.

clue.text: Relaxed with cryptic setter in secure comfort

parts.note: relaxed and easy both mean free from tension

indicators.note: something cryptic is puzzling and disguised, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, relaxed and cryptic, living a comfortable, settled life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cryptic' looks like it describes the setter but is the anagram signal; 'in' is part of the idiom, not an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in financial security and comfort.

clue.text: Republican sort who leads a dull life — one's often seen pickled

parts.note: in US politics red is the colour of the Republican Party

parts.words: sort who leads a dull life
parts.note: a cabbage is informally a person who lives an inactive, dull existence

explanation.surface: A dreary Republican who is frequently found drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pickled' looks like a slang word for drunk, describing the dull Republican; it is literal, the vegetable preserved in vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: This purple brassica is commonly preserved in vinegar and sold in jars, so it is often seen pickled.

clue.text: British booze in bound bundle

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, so booze

explanation.surface: British alcohol packed into a tied-up parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay, straw or cotton is pressed and tied into a bale, a large bound bundle.

clue.text: Mostly fast to lift those inevitable outcomes of austerity

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters reads them from bottom to top, backwards
mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: fast and stuck both mean firmly fixed in place

explanation.surface: Austerity hurts: a plea to quickly raise spirits against its unavoidable effects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims STUCK to STUC, and 'to lift' turns that upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerity programmes mean reductions in public spending, which are spending reductions, so the plural noun fits.

clue.text: Boss who believes he can keep it up

definitions.meaning: a boss is a knob or raised ornament

definitions.text: who believes he can keep it up
definitions.meaning: a man who fancies himself sexually prolific; also a stallion kept for breeding

explanation.surface: A manager full of confidence that he can sustain his performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss and a stud are both raised knobs; a stud is also slang for a virile, sexually confident man.

clue.text: Thief's opening sack for something and nothing?

indicators.note: the opening of the thief's name is its first letter

parts.note: to sack a place is to plunder it, which is to rifle it

explanation.surface: A burglar starts by ransacking for anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something and nothing' is a phrase for an unimportant matter; the question mark hints at the pudding too.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a matter of little importance, something that amounts to almost nothing.

clue.text: Who's busy covering conflict in cave?

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the second, covering it on both sides

parts.note: busy as a bee: the bee is the proverbial busy one
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Asking which creature is busy keeping a fight hidden inside a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' looks like a hollow in rock; it is the Latin warning (pronounced KAY-vee) once shouted by schoolboys as a lookout's alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is Latin schoolboy slang shouted as a warning, so it means look out.

clue.text: This upset true lady

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something has distressed a faithful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes what would upset a true lady: her partner's infidelity.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithfulness in marriage is what would distress a loyal wife, so the whole clue points to it.

clue.text: Cheerful daughter avoiding butter, say

indicators.note: avoiding means the letter for daughter is left out

parts.note: butter is an example of a dairy product
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A happy girl who steers clear of butter, perhaps while dieting.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can describe a light-hearted, breezy, carefree manner, close to cheerful.

clue.text: Shed near Derby, for example, makes you depressed

indicators.note: near places the word for shed right beside the example of Derby

parts.note: Derby is a type of English cheese
to doff is to take off, or shed, clothing

explanation.surface: An outbuilding beside Derby is enough to make anyone feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a garden hut and 'Derby' a town; Derby is a mild English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for fed up or annoyed, so feeling down.

clue.text: What's owed by one breaking out? Tons

parts.note: a deb or debutante is a young woman coming out into society

explanation.surface: Asking what an escaping prisoner owes, and answering: a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' suggests a jailbreak; here it is a debutante making her debut, or coming out, in society.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money or a favour owed to someone else.

clue.text: Stern, tough old bird that gets you in hot water?

definitions.text: that gets you in hot water?

parts.note: the stern of a boat is its back
a boiler is an old hen only fit for boiling; also slang for an unattractive older woman

explanation.surface: A severe old woman who lands you in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hot water' means in trouble; here it is literal, as a back boiler sits behind a fireplace heating water.
explanation.definitionFit: A back boiler is a domestic water heater fitted behind a fire, so it supplies hot water.

clue.text: Fruit juice fortified by wine, dad's restorative?

parts.note: a cup is a punch-like drink of fruit juice mixed with wine, such as claret cup
pa is dad; the apostrophe s is just the possessive of the surface

explanation.surface: Father's pick-me-up is a fruity drink spiked with wine.
explanation.walkthrough: A cuppa is British informal for a cup of tea, the classic pick-me-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup of tea is the traditional British reviver, so it is offered as a restorative, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A not wholly reliable ticket agency can split

definitions.text: A not wholly reliable ticket agency

parts.note: a can or pail is a bucket
to split on someone is to inform on them, which in British slang is to shop them

explanation.surface: A dodgy ticket seller who may disappear with your money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can split' reads as able to leave; can is a container and split means inform.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket shop is an agency selling cheap air tickets, often seen as unreliable or shady.

clue.text: Shilly-shallying Tories rule in topsy- turvy fashion

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down and jumbled, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The Conservatives govern chaotically and indecisively.
explanation.definitionFit: Shilly-shallying is dithering, the hallmark of being unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Instrument of early recordings

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken from within the words that follow, made of their letters

explanation.surface: An instrument heard on the first sound recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed instrument, a small harp.

clue.text: Jelly's about flavour being slightly reduced

parts.note: A is an abbreviation of about, approximately

indicators.note: slightly reduced means one letter, the last, is cut off

parts.note: spice is something added for flavour

explanation.surface: A jelly whose taste has been toned down a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Upon which Huck Finn went to shop, fellow admitted

indicators.note: admitted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to shop someone is to betray them, to rat on them

explanation.surface: Huck Finn set off to a store, and a man was let in.
explanation.walkthrough: In Mark Twain's novel, Huckleberry Finn travels down the Mississippi on a raft.
explanation.definitionFit: Huckleberry Finn floats down the Mississippi on a timber platform with Jim, a raft.

clue.text: Disgraceful family doyenne in residence

indicators.note: in places the grandmother inside the home

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a residence
the gran or grandmother is often the senior woman of a family

explanation.surface: A shocking matriarch living at the family home.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly offensive, so conspicuously disgraceful.

clue.text: In leather gal shocked

indicators.note: shocked means violently disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman dressed in leather is scandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition; it is the adjective meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In means fashionable and popular, the same sense as the trendy phrase for the latest craze.

clue.text: Comparatively generous Rector surrounded by drink

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the rector inside the drink

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer

explanation.surface: A clergyman in the pub, generous after a few drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means generous in size, so the comparative form means more generous.

clue.text: Game is beginning to settle down

indicators.note: the beginning of settle is its first letter

parts.note: nap is the soft raised pile on cloth, like down

explanation.surface: A sporting contest is starting to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle down' reads as calm down; down is soft fluff, NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game where matching cards are spotted by calling out.

clue.text: The mark of pirate mix remains

parts.note: a cross is a mix or hybrid of two breeds
bones are a body's remains

explanation.surface: A pirate's sign mixes together human remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull and crossbones is the symbol on the pirate flag, the Jolly Roger.

clue.text: Short chap filing hard copy

indicators.note: filing means walking into in a line, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Sam is a short form of Samuel, a man's name
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A little man in an office filing a printed version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard copy' reads as a printout; hard is H and copy is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake, an imitation or copy passed off as genuine.

clue.text: Force barrel price up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: Forcing the price of a barrel of oil higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for muscle, strength or power, so force.

clue.text: Out to lunch? Turn bowl over

indicators.note: turn means the letters are turned round to run the other way

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to astonish them, to stun them

explanation.surface: A mealtime break, then an instruction to tip a dish upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to lunch' reads as gone for a meal; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Out to lunch is slang for mad or eccentric, and so is nuts.

clue.text: Romp with high-flying singer

definitions.meaning: a romp is a bit of fun or a frolic, a spree
the skylark is a songbird that sings while flying high

explanation.surface: Fooling about with a successful pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a bit of mischief, and also the bird famous for singing as it soars.

clue.text: A negative effect at the end of last month's declining

indicators.note: at the end of places the following pieces after the month

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
a dent is a negative effect, as in a dent in profits

explanation.surface: An unfavourable result at the end of the previous month's slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means in a state of moral or cultural decline.

clue.text: Going for work before the sound of bell

indicators.note: before puts the work first and the bell sound after it

parts.note: OP, short for opus, means a musical work
ting is the ringing sound of a small bell

explanation.surface: Heading to work before the bell rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Opting for something is choosing it, so going for it.
